summary: Cleantech Open has current official 2026 U.S. Accelerator information. Applications are now closed; the 2026 cohort launched May 28-29 and culminates at Global Forum/National Finals in October.

proposed_event.name: Cleantech Open US Accelerator 2026
proposed_event.description: U.S. cleantech accelerator with mentoring, workshops, showcases and prize/investment opportunities.

dates.date_range_text: 2026 cohort: final application deadline April 6; National Academy May 28-29 in New York City; Global Forum/National Finals October 20-22 in Boston, culminating October 22 at Greentown Labs in Somerville.

sources.title: Cleantech Open 2026 CTO Accelerator
sources.supports: Official 2026 accelerator page supports benefits, 12-week workshops, prize/investment opportunities, eligibility, April 6 final deadline, May acceptance timing, required National Academy May 28-29 in New York City, and Global Forum/National Finals October 20-22 in Boston.

sources.title: Cleantech Open National homepage
sources.supports: Official homepage states Cleantech Open runs the largest clean technology accelerator program, links to the 2026 Accelerator page, and says applications are closed.

sources.title: Alliance for Climate Transition Welcomes 2026 Cleantech Open Northeast Cohort
sources.supports: Official June 2026 news post confirms the 2026 cohort is underway, launched May 28-29 at National Academy in Brooklyn, runs as a six-month accelerator, has September regional judging, and culminates October 22 at Global Forum Showcase and Awards Celebration at Greentown Labs in Somerville, MA.

notes: Applications are closed as of 2026-06-09, so the record is shaped as the current 2026 cohort rather than an open application opportunity.

The official accelerator page includes some generic FAQ text with older examples, but the 2026-specific dates are clearly stated in the requirements section and corroborated by the June 2026 official news post.
The program is national/regional with required in-person events, so location is represented at the U.S. level with hybrid participation rather than a single city.
